def from_json(self, json_str: str) -> None:
    """Load the state from a JSON string."""
    data = json.loads(json_str)
    mtemp = data.get("models", [])
    self.models = {}
    if mtemp:
        for model in mtemp:
            self.add_model(Model(**model), emit_events=False)
            m_id = uuid.UUID(model["id"])
            self.models[m_id].components = [Component(**comp) for comp in model.get("components", [])]
            self.models[m_id].binding_constants = [BindingConstant(**k) for k in model.get("binding_constants", [])]
            self.models[m_id].eq_mat = np.array(model.get("eq_mat", []))  # Convert numpy arrays to lists
            self.models[m_id].component_concs = pd.DataFrame(model.get("component_concs", {}))

    self.simulations = {}
    simtemp = data.get("simulations", [])
    if simtemp:
        for sim in simtemp:
            simulation = Simulation(**sim)
            simulation.model_id = uuid.UUID(sim.get("model_id"))
            simulation.comp_concs = pd.DataFrame(sim.get("comp_concs", {}))
            # simulation.model = Model(**sim.get("model", {}))
            # simulation.params = [BindingConstant(**k) for k in sim.get('params', [])]
            simulation.results = pd.DataFrame(sim.get("results", {}))
            self.simulations[simulation.id] = simulation

    self.fits = {}
    fittemp = data.get("fits", [])  # List of fits
    if fittemp:
        for fit in fittemp:
            # backward compatibility to load pre-0.1.7 fits
            fit.pop("analytical_obs_columns",None)
            fit.pop("analytical_obs_components",None)
            fit_result = FitResult(**fit)
            fit_result.fit_speciation = pd.DataFrame(fit.get("fit_speciation", {}))
            fit_result.calc_obs = pd.DataFrame(fit.get("calc_obs", {}))
            self.fits[fit_result.id] = fit_result

    self.mcmcs = {}
    mcmc_temp = data.get("mcmcs", [])
    if mcmc_temp:
        for mcmc in mcmc_temp:
            try:
                mcmc_obj = MCMCSim(**mcmc)
                if not isinstance(mcmc_obj.chains, np.ndarray):
                    mcmc_obj.chains = np.array(mcmc_obj.chains)
                mcmc_obj.model_id = self._normalize_uuid(mcmc_obj.model_id)
                mcmc_obj.expt_data_id = self._normalize_uuid(mcmc_obj.expt_data_id)
                self.mcmcs[mcmc_obj.id] = mcmc_obj
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Skipping invalid serialized MCMC entry: {e}")

    rawtemp = data.get("raw_datas", [])  # List of raw data
    self.raw_datas = {}
    if rawtemp:
        for raw in rawtemp:
            raw_data = RawData(**raw)
            raw_data.data = pd.DataFrame(raw.get("data", {}))
            self.raw_datas[raw_data.id] = raw_data  # Store by UUID

    expttemp = data.get("expt_datas", [])  # List of experimental data
    self.expt_datas = {}
    if expttemp:
        for expt in expttemp:
            # Ensure backward compatibility - add selected_columns if missing
            if "selected_columns" not in expt:
                expt["selected_columns"] = []

            expt_data = ExptData(**expt)
            # limiting_shifts now serialized as list of ChemicalShiftParam dicts
            expt_data.limiting_shifts = {}
            for cs in expt.get("limiting_shifts", []) or []:
                csp = ChemicalShiftParam(**cs)
                key = (csp.species, csp.col)
                expt_data.limiting_shifts[key] = csp

            # Reconstruct delta_to_spec (object ndarray with floats or lmfit Parameters)
            serialized_delta = expt.get("delta_to_spec", [])
            if serialized_delta == []:
                expt_data.delta_to_spec = None
            elif isinstance(serialized_delta, list) and serialized_delta:
                # Expect a list of rows
                new_rows: list[list[LMFitParameter | float]] = []
                for row in serialized_delta:
                    reconstructed_row: list[LMFitParameter | float] = []
                    for cell in row:
                        if isinstance(cell, dict) and cell.get("type") == "lmfit_param":
                            # Construct lmfit Parameter
                            parameter = LMFitParameter(
                                name=cell.get("name", ""),
                                value=float(cell.get("value", 0.0)),
                            )
                            if cell.get("min") is not None:
                                parameter.min = float(cell["min"])  # type: ignore[index]
                            if cell.get("max") is not None:
                                parameter.max = float(cell["max"])  # type: ignore[index]
                            parameter.vary = bool(cell.get("vary", True))
                            reconstructed_row.append(parameter)
                        elif cell is None:
                            reconstructed_row.append(None)
                        elif isinstance(cell, (str, int, float)):
                            try:
                                reconstructed_row.append(float(cell))
                            except Exception:
                                logger.warning(f"Failed to convert cell {cell} to float, appending 0.0")
                                reconstructed_row.append(0.0)
                    new_rows.append(reconstructed_row)
                try:
                    nr = len(new_rows)
                    nc = len(new_rows[0]) if nr > 0 else 0
                    # Attempt to create a 2D numpy array with dtype=object
                    # need to do this long-winded approach to stop numpy from
                    # trying (and failing) to coerce the object array to a float array
                    # which calls Parameter.__array__ and fails.
                    if nc > 0:
                        expt_data.delta_to_spec = np.empty((nr, nc), dtype=object)
                        for i in range(nr):
                            for j in range(nc):
                                expt_data.delta_to_spec[i, j] = new_rows[i][j]
                    # expt_data.delta_to_spec = np.array(new_rows, dtype=object)
                except Exception:
                    # If object array fails, still set as object array coercing to objects
                    expt_data.delta_to_spec = np.array([[x for x in row] for row in new_rows], dtype=object)
            self.expt_datas[expt_data.id] = expt_data

    self._nComp = int(data.get("nComp", 2))
    self._nStep = int(data.get("nStep", 20))
    self._eq_str = data.get("eq_str", "")
    self._eq_mat_str = data.get("eq_mat_str", "[]")
    self._eq_mat = np.array(data.get("eq_mat", []))
    comp_temp = data.get("components", [])
    self._components = [Component(**comp) for comp in comp_temp] if comp_temp else []
    ktemp = data.get("binding_constants", [])
    self._binding_constants = [BindingConstant(**k) for k in ktemp] if ktemp else []
    self._species = data.get("species", [])
    self._eq_consts = data.get("eq_consts", None)
    self._model_name = data.get("model_name", "")
    self._component_names = data.get("component_names", [])
    self._comp_concs = pd.DataFrame(data.get("comp_concs", {}))
    self._expt_data = ExptData(**data.get("expt_data", {}))
    self._active_model_id = self._normalize_uuid(data.get("active_model_id", None))
    self._active_sim_id = self._normalize_uuid(data.get("active_sim_id", None))
    self._active_fit_id = self._normalize_uuid(data.get("active_fit_id", None))
    self._active_raw_data_id = self._normalize_uuid(data.get("active_raw_data_id", None))
    self._active_expt_data_id = self._normalize_uuid(data.get("active_expt_data_id", None))
    self._active_mcmc_id = self._normalize_uuid(data.get("active_mcmc_id", None))

    mids = data.get("default_model_ids", None)
    if mids:
        self.default_model_ids = [uuid.UUID(m) for m in mids]
    else:
        # Backward compatibility for older saved states without default_model_ids.
        # Any model ID that matches the bundled defaults is treated as built-in.
        bundled_default_ids = self._default_model_ids_from_bundle()
        self.default_model_ids = [mid for mid in self.models.keys() if mid in bundled_default_ids]

    # self._active_raw_data_id = data.get("active_raw_data_id", None)
    for name, dtype in data.get("_expt_dtypes", {}).items():
        self._expt_dtypes[name] = ExptDataType(**dtype)

    self._finalize_active_context(reason="from_json", emit_events=False)

def generate_binding_constants(self):
    """Generate binding constants based on the current model."""
    if not self.active_model:
        ui.notify("No active model to generate binding constants.", type="negative")
        return

    species = self.active_model.species
    components = self.active_model.component_names

    # number of bound species:
    boundspecies = [s for s in species if s not in components]
    # num_bound_species = len(species) - len(components)

    for s in species:
        if s not in [k.species for k in self.active_model.binding_constants if k.species not in species]:
            logK = None
            isComp = False
            vary = True
            if s not in boundspecies:
                # this is a component so logK = 0
                logK = 0
                isComp = True
                vary = False
            self.active_model.binding_constants.append(
                BindingConstant(species=s, logK=logK, vary=vary, isComp=isComp)
            )

    # remove stale binding constants
    # self.sd.binding_constants = [k for k in self.sd.binding_constants if k.species in species]

    # ensure isComp is set correctly for existing binding constants, and remove stale ones
    for k in self.active_model.binding_constants:
        if k.species not in species:
            self.active_model.binding_constants.remove(k)
        else:
            if k.species in components:
                k.isComp = True
            else:
                k.isComp = False

    # reorder self.sd.binding_constants to match species list
    ro = []
    for s in species:
        # as a quick check, ensure components have logK=0
        for k in self.active_model.binding_constants:
            if k.species in components:
                k.logK = 0
            # reorder self.sd.binding_constants to match species list
        ro.append([k for k in self.active_model.binding_constants if k.species == s][0])

    self.active_model.binding_constants = ro

def generate_binding_model_for_fit(
    self,
    fit: Optional[FitResult] = None,
    analytical_cfg: Optional[dict[str, object]] = None,
    force_numerical: bool = False,
) -> bd.bindingModel:
    """Generate a bindtools.bindingModel from the current active model."""
    old_fit = None
    if fit is not None and fit.id != self.active_fit_id:
        old_fit = str(self.active_fit_id)
        self.active_fit_id = fit.id
        self.active_expt_data_id = fit.expt_data_id
        self.active_model_id = fit.model_id

    if not self.active_model:
        raise ValueError("No active model to generate binding model.")

    obs_list = [
        x
        for x in self.active_expt_data.sorted_data.columns
        if self.active_expt_data.col_details[x]["depindep"] == "dep"
    ]
    integ_to_spec = self.active_expt_data.integ_to_spec
    if not (isinstance(integ_to_spec, np.ndarray) and integ_to_spec.ndim == 2 and integ_to_spec.size > 0):
        integ_to_spec = None
    delta_to_spec = self.active_expt_data.delta_to_spec
    if not (isinstance(delta_to_spec, np.ndarray) and delta_to_spec.ndim == 2 and delta_to_spec.size > 0):
        delta_to_spec = None

    model = bd.bindingModel(
        eqMat=self.active_model.eq_mat,
        compNames=self.active_model.component_names,
        speciesList=self.active_model.species,
        colToComp=self.active_expt_data.col_to_comp,
        specToInteg=integ_to_spec,
        specToDd=delta_to_spec.T if delta_to_spec is not None else None,
        obsList=obs_list,
        rawData=np.array(self.active_expt_data.sorted_data),
    )

    cfg = analytical_cfg
    if cfg is None and fit is not None and getattr(fit, "analytical_fast_exchange", False):
        cfg = {
            "topology": fit.analytical_topology,
            "complex_indices": list(getattr(fit, "analytical_complex_indices", [])),
        }

    if cfg is not None:
        model.analytical_fast_exchange = True
        model.analytical_topology = str(cfg["topology"])
        model.analytical_complex_indices = [int(x) for x in cfg["complex_indices"]]  # type: ignore[index]
        logger.info(
            "Using analytical fast-exchange backend (%s model) for fitting.",
            model.analytical_topology,
        )

    # Handle UV-vis / fluorescence linear observables (numerical and analytical paths).
    if self.active_expt_data.has_linear_obs(self._expt_dtypes):
        self.active_expt_data.build_abs_to_spec(self._expt_dtypes)
        abs_to_spec = self.active_expt_data.abs_to_spec
        if (
            abs_to_spec is not None
            and isinstance(abs_to_spec, np.ndarray)
            and abs_to_spec.ndim == 2
            and abs_to_spec.size > 0
        ):
            model.specToLinear = abs_to_spec.T  # (n_species, n_obs)

            # Build per-observable param name map for the analytical path.
            linear_obs_param_map: list[list] = []
            for obs_idx in range(abs_to_spec.shape[0]):
                pnames: list = []
                for species_idx in range(abs_to_spec.shape[1]):
                    cell = abs_to_spec[obs_idx, species_idx]
                    pnames.append(cell.name if isinstance(cell, LMFitParameter) else None)
                linear_obs_param_map.append(pnames)

            lin_cols = [
                col
                for col in obs_list
                if self.active_expt_data.col_details.get(col, {}).get("depindep") == "dep"
                # already filtered above — just iterate obs_list directly
            ]
            model.analytical_linear_obs_columns = lin_cols
            model.analytical_linear_obs_param_map = linear_obs_param_map

    model.prepModel(force_numerical=force_numerical)

    for k in self.active_model.binding_constants:
        model.params[f"log{k.species}"].set(
            value=k.logK if k.logK is not None else 0.0, vary=k.vary, min=k.min, max=k.max
        )

    # cleanup by restoring previous fit if needed
    if old_fit is not None:
        self.active_fit_id = uuid.UUID(old_fit)
        self.active_expt_data_id = self.active_fit.expt_data_id
        self.active_model_id = self.active_fit.model_id

    return model

async def parse_equations(self, e):
    """Parse the equilibrium equations and update the model data output."""

    # if current model_name is already a model, ask the user if they want to overwrite
    if self.model_name in [m.name for m in self.models.values()]:
        # model = [m for m in self.models if m.name == self.model_name][0]
        model = self.active_model
        if model.eq_mat_str == "" or model.eq_mat is np.array([]):
            # then this is a new model and we don't need to ask about overwriting
            pass
        # otherwise, we need to ask the user if they want to overwrite the model
        else:
            with ui.dialog() as dialog, ui.card():
                ui.label(
                    f'Are you sure you want to overwrite model "{self.model_name}"? \nDoing so will delete all simulations and fits which rely on this model.'
                )
                with ui.row():
                    ui.button("Yes", on_click=lambda: dialog.submit(True))
                    ui.button("No", on_click=lambda: dialog.submit(False))

            async def show():
                result = await dialog
                return result

            res = await show()
            if res is False:  # i.e. user does not want to save
                ui.notify("Please give a unique model name and re-try.", type="info")
                return
            else:
                ui.notify(f"Overwriting model {self.model_name}", type="warning")

    eq_input = self.active_model.eq_str.strip() if self.active_model.eq_str else ""

    if not eq_input:
        ui.notify("Please enter equilibrium equations.", type="negative")
        return
    try:
        eq_matrix, component_names, species = eq_mat_from_equation_str_infer_components(eq_input)
        model = self.active_model
        nmodel = len(self.models)
        self.delete_model(self.active_model, notify_user=False, notify_listeners=True)
        if nmodel == 1:
            # if  we had only one model, then deletion would have initialized a default model
            # since we cannot have zero models.
            self.active_model.name = model.name  # Set the name of the default model
        else:
            self.new_model(name=model.name)  # Create a new model with the same name
        self.active_model.eq_str = model.eq_str  # Copy the equilibrium string from the old model
        self.active_model.nComp = model.nComp  # Copy the number of components from the old model
        self.active_model.nStep = model.nStep  # Copy the number of steps from the
        self.active_model.component_concs = (
            model.component_concs
        )  # Copy the component concentrations from the old model
        self.active_model.component_names = model.component_names  # Copy the component names from the old model
        self.active_model.components = model.components  # Copy the components from the old model
        # self.notify_listeners('model_changed')  # Notify listeners that the model has been updated
        # self.active_model_idx = self.models.index(model)

        self.active_model.eq_mat = eq_matrix
        # TODO replace next line with a property
        self.active_model.eq_mat_str = str(eq_matrix.tolist()).replace("],", "]\n")  # Convert to list for display
        self.species = species
        self.component_names = component_names

        self.active_model.nComp = len(component_names)  # Update number of components in SimData
        #    self.modelData.set_visibility(True)  # Show the model data output area

        for comp in component_names:
            if comp not in [comp.name for comp in self.components]:
                # Add new component to SimData
                self.components.append(Component(name=comp))

        self.components = [
            comp for comp in self.components if comp.name in component_names
        ]  # Keep only components that are in the list

        # reorder sd.components to match components list, based on the name attribute of sd.components elements
        self.components = sorted(
            self.components,
            key=lambda x: component_names.index(x.name) if x.name in component_names else float("inf"),
        )

        self.generate_binding_constants()  # Generate binding constants based on the current model

        self.notify_listeners(
            "model_changed", self.active_model
        )  # Notify listeners that the model has been updated

        # Disable save button when equations are parsed
        # TODO restore #self.save_sim_details_button.set_enabled(False)
        # default to model name + values of Ks

    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(e)
        ui.notify("Error: " + str(e), type="negative")

docs.title: Quick Workflow Summary
docs.text:
1. Launch bindmc via standalone binary, python -m bindmc, or python main.py.
  2. Go to Binding Models to enter stoichiometric equilibrium equations (e.g., H + G <=> HG).
  3. Navigate to Data Import to load titration data (CSV/Excel).
  4. Select Fitting to optimize binding constants (\(K\)) and physical parameters (\(\delta\)).
  5. Run Bayesian MCMC to generate posterior probability distributions and corner plots.
  6. Click Export Notebook in the header to download a reproducible .ipynb Jupyter notebook.

docs.title: Bayesian MCMC Sampling
docs.text: The Bayes / MCMC tab performs Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling using emcee to sample the posterior probability distribution of model parameters, quantifying uncertainties and parameter correlations.

docs.title: 1. Prior Distributions & Parameter Bounds
docs.text:
In bindmc, parameters are assigned Uniform priors bounded by lower and upper limits \([a, b]\):

\[P(\theta) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{b - a} & \text{if } a \le \theta \le b \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\]

Parameter bounds (e.g., restricting \(\log_{10} K \in [0, 14]\) or limiting chemical shifts \(\delta\)) prevent non-physical regions of parameter space during sampling.

docs.title: 2. Heterogeneous Experimental Weighting (lnsigma)
docs.text:
When combining multiple data types or techniques (e.g. NMR chemical shifts in ppm vs. UV-Vis absorbance in AU vs. NMR peak integrations), measurement uncertainties and units differ significantly.

bindmc automatically creates and samples independent log-variance hyperparameters (\(\ln \sigma\)) for each experimental technique: - lnsigmadeltaH (NMR \(^1\text{H}\) shifts) - lnsigmadeltaF (NMR \(^{19}\text{F}\) shifts) - lnsigmaUVvis (UV-Vis absorbance) - lnsigmaFluorescence (Fluorescence intensity) - lnsigmaNMRInteg (NMR peak integrations)

This ensures that heterogeneous datasets are appropriately weighted according to their individual noise characteristics without manual scaling.

docs.title: 3. Convergence Diagnostics (\(\tau\))
docs.text:
• Walkers: Number of MCMC ensemble walkers (typically \(32\) to \(64\)).
  • Integrated Autocorrelation Time (\(\tau\)): bindmc estimates the integrated autocorrelation time \(\tau\) for each parameter chain. As a rule of thumb, sampling should run for at least \(50 \times \tau\) steps to guarantee independent samples and converged chains.
  • Trace Plots: Inspect parameter values vs. step index across all walkers. Converged chains resemble stable, stationary "hairy caterpillars" without long-term drift.

docs.title: Option A: Jupyter Notebook Export (Recommended)
docs.text: Click Export Notebook in the top navigation header to download an executable .ipynb notebook alongside your .h5 MCMC session. The exported notebook includes complete, pre-configured template plotting code using arviz, corner, and matplotlib.

docs.title: Option B: Custom Python Analysis Script
docs.text:
You can also inspect raw MCMC chains directly from exported .h5 files in Python:

import h5py
import numpy as np
import corner
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Open exported HDF5 session file
with h5py.File("mcmc_session.h5", "r") as f:
    chain = f["mcmc/chain"][:]        # Shape: (steps, walkers, n_params)
    log_prob = f["mcmc/log_prob"][:]  # Log posterior probabilities
    labels = [s.decode() if isinstance(s, bytes) else str(s) for s in f["mcmc"].attrs["labels"]]

# 2. Discard burn-in (e.g., first 200 steps) and flatten chains
burn_in = 200
flat_chain = chain[burn_in:].reshape(-1, chain.shape[-1])

# 3. Generate publication-ready Corner plot
fig = corner.corner(
    flat_chain,
    labels=labels,
    show_titles=True,
    quantiles=[0.16, 0.50, 0.84],
    title_fmt=".2f"
)
plt.savefig("mcmc_corner_plot.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()

docs.title: Binding Models & Speciation Solvers
docs.text: bindmc supports two modes for calculating equilibrium species concentrations: 1. Numerical Speciation Solver: Arbitrary stoichiometries using Newton–Raphson iteration. 2. Analytical Fast Exchange Solvers: Exact closed-form algebraic solutions for common single host-guest topologies (\(1:1\), \(1:2\), \(2:1\)).

docs.title: 1. Numerical Solver (Newton–Raphson)
docs.text:
The general chemical equilibrium for formation of complex species \(C_j\) from \(N\) components \(A_i\) is described by:

\[a_{j1} A_1 + a_{j2} A_2 + \dots + a_{jN} A_N \rightleftharpoons C_j\]

with cumulative formation constant \(\beta_j = 10^{\log_{10} K_j}\):

\[[C_j] = \beta_j \prod_{i=1}^N [A_i]^{a_{ji}}\]

The mass balance equations for each component total concentration \(T_i\) are:

\[T_i = [A_i] + \sum_{j} a_{ji} [C_j]\]

bindmc uses bindtools.binding.DoNR, a Numba-JIT compiled Newton–Raphson solver with analytical Jacobian evaluation, ensuring high-speed calculation across thousands of titration points.

docs.title: Writing Equations in the GUI
docs.text:
In the Binding Model tab, enter equilibrium reactions directly using standard chemical notation:

H + G <=> HG
H + 2G <=> HG2

bindmc automatically parses the equations, identifies free components (H, G) and complexes (HG, HG2), and constructs the stoichiometry matrix (\(E_{\text{mat}}\)).

docs.title: 2. Analytical Fast-Exchange Solvers
docs.text:
For fast-exchange titrations with standard binding topologies (\(1:1\), \(1:2\), \(2:1\) host-guest systems), analytical solvers avoid iterative root-finding overhead.

bindmc automatically inspects the stoichiometry matrix (\(E_{\text{mat}}\)) to detect whether a model matches a simple analytical topology. If it does, calc_analytical_speciation calculates exact species concentrations in a single vectorized numpy operation.

docs.title: 1:1 Fast Exchange Model
docs.text:
Equilibrium reaction: \(\text{H} + \text{G} \rightleftharpoons \text{HG}\) with binding constant \(K_{11}\).

Free guest concentration \([G]\) is solved directly via quadratic formula:

\[K_{11} [G]^2 + (1 + K_{11} [\text{H}]_{\text{tot}} - K_{11} [\text{G}]_{\text{tot}}) [G] - [\text{G}]_{\text{tot}} = 0\]

Observed chemical shift:

\[\delta_{\text{obs}} = \delta_{\text{H}} + (\delta_{\text{HG}} - \delta_{\text{H}}) \frac{[\text{HG}]}{[\text{H}]_{\text{tot}}}\]

docs.title: 1:2 and 2:1 Fast Exchange Models
docs.text: Closed-form analytical equations solve cubic polynomials directly via vectorized trigonometric methods (_solve_cubic_vectorized).

docs.title: Data Import & Schemas
docs.text: bindmc supports importing experimental titration data from CSV (.csv) and Excel (.xlsx, .xls) files.

docs.title: File Layout Standards
docs.text: Your data file should structure data in columns where each row represents a single titration point (e.g. single tube or addition step).

docs.title: Experimental Data Types
docs.text: When assigning columns in the Data Import tab, select the correct Experimental Data Type:

docs.title: 1. NMR Chemical Shifts (deltaH / deltaF)
docs.text:
• Fast Exchange: Observed chemical shift \(\delta_{\text{obs}}\) is the mole-fraction weighted average of free species and complexes: $\(\delta_{\text{obs}} = \sum_{i} x_i \cdot \delta_i\)$ where \(x_i = \frac{c_i}{C_{\text{total\_host}}}\) is the fraction of host present in species \(i\).
  • Parametric Binding Constants: Each species \(i\) has an associated chemical shift parameter \(\delta_i\).

docs.title: 2. UV-Vis / Fluorescence Absorbance (absorbance / fluorescence)
docs.text: • Linear concentration-weighted observables (Beer-Lambert law): $\(A_{\text{obs}} = \sum_{i} \varepsilon_i \cdot c_i \cdot l\)$ where \(\varepsilon_i\) is the molar extinction coefficient / fluorescence intensity factor for species \(i\).

docs.title: 3. Peak Integrations (integration)
docs.text: • Peak integration areas proportional to concentrations of specific species (slow exchange NMR or HPLC peak areas).

docs.title: Mapping Columns in bindmc
docs.text:
1. Click Choose File in the Data Import tab.
  2. Select your CSV or Excel file.
  3. For each component defined in your model (e.g. H, G), select the corresponding dataset column for total concentration (\([\text{H}]_{\text{tot}}\), \([\text{G}]_{\text{tot}}\)).
  4. Add dependent variable series, giving each a name (e.g., Peak H1) and assigning its data column and observable type.

docs.title: Non-Linear Fitting
docs.text: The Fitting tab optimizes binding constants (\(\log_{10} K\)) and physical observable parameters (e.g. chemical shifts \(\delta\), extinction coefficients \(\varepsilon\)) against imported titration data using lmfit.

docs.title: 1. Minimizer Algorithm Selection
docs.text:
bindmc provides access to several optimization algorithms depending on model complexity and parameter conditioning:

Algorithm Name Method Key in lmfit Recommended Usage Levenberg-Marquardt (Default) least_squares / lm Standard non-linear least squares. Fastest convergence for well-behaved problems with smooth gradients. L-BFGS-B lbfgsb Bounded quasi-Newton optimization. Ideal when strict parameter bounds are required and gradient evaluation is cheap. Nelder-Mead nelder-mead Simplex direct-search method. Gradient-free optimization useful when residual landscapes are noisy or non-smooth. AMPGO ampgo Adaptive Memory Programming for Global Optimization. Useful for exploring complex multimodal parameter spaces with multiple local minima.

docs.title: 2. Weighting & Technique-Specific Errors
docs.text:
When fitting single data series, residuals are evaluated as:

\[\text{residual}_i = \frac{y_{\text{exp}, i} - y_{\text{fit}, i}}{\sigma}\]
  • Single Dataset Weighting: For single-technique fits, uniform weighting (\(\sigma = 1\)) optimizes unweighted sum of squared residuals.
  • Heterogeneous Data: Note that when combining multiple experimental techniques (e.g., NMR ppm shifts alongside UV-Vis absorbance), each technique operates on different units and scales. In bindmc, technique-specific error variance parameters (\(\ln \sigma\)) are modeled explicitly during Bayesian MCMC sampling to prevent larger numerical units from dominating the optimization.

docs.title: 3. Parameter Constraints & Bounds
docs.text:
• Initial Guesses: Enter starting estimates for \(\log_{10} K\) values (e.g. \(3.5\) for \(K \approx 3,160 \text{ M}^{-1}\)).
  • Vary / Fix Flags: Toggle checkboxes to hold known parameters fixed (e.g., free host chemical shift \(\delta_{\text{H}}\) measured independently prior to titration).
  • Lower / Upper Bounds: Restrict parameter ranges to physically meaningful bounds (e.g., \(\log_{10}K \ge 0\)).

docs.title: 4. Fitting Diagnostics & Troubleshooting
docs.text: After optimization completes, bindmc displays parameter standard errors (\(1\sigma\)) and correlation coefficients:

docs.title: High Parameter Correlation (\(r > 0.95\))
docs.text:
• Cause: Strong correlation between two parameters (e.g. binding constant \(\log_{10} K\) and bound complex chemical shift \(\delta_{\text{HG}}\) in weak binding regimes where \(K [\text{H}]_{\text{tot}} \ll 1\)).
  • Solution: Measure the free component property (\(\delta_{\text{H}}\) or \(\varepsilon_{\text{H}}\)) independently and fix it in the model, or increase maximum titrant concentration to reach saturation.

docs.title: Non-Convergence or Boundary Clipping
docs.text:
• Symptom: Parameter pegged exactly at lower or upper bound, or high standard errors (\(> 100\%\)).
  • Solution: Try switching minimizer to nelder-mead or ampgo to escape local minima, or expand parameter bounds.

docs.title: Notebook Export & Reproducibility
docs.text: bindmc emphasizes open science and complete analytical reproducibility. At any point in your workflow, you can export your session to a standalone, executable Jupyter Notebook (.ipynb).

docs.title: How to Export
docs.text:
1. Complete your data import, model setup, and/or non-linear fitting in the bindmc web GUI.
  2. In the top navigation header, click Export Notebook.
  3. Save the generated .ipynb file to your local computer.

docs.title: What the Exported Notebook Contains
docs.text:
The exported Jupyter Notebook is completely self-contained and standalone:

  • Raw Data Ingestion: Recreates the experimental titration data arrays directly in Python code.
  • Stoichiometry Matrix: Reconstructs the equilibrium species equations and stoichiometry matrix.
  • bindtools API Invocation: Imports bindtools and sets up lmfit minimization parameters matching your exact GUI state.
  • Publication-Ready Figures: Generates high-resolution Matplotlib figure code for titration fit curves, residual plots, speciation diagrams, and corner plots.

docs.title: Running the Exported Notebook
docs.text:
Open the notebook in Jupyter Lab, VS Code, or Google Colab:

jupyter lab my_bindmc_fit.ipynb

Executing all cells reproduces your exact numerical fitting results, standard errors, and plots independently of the GUI application.

docs.title: User Guide Overview
docs.text: bindmc provides an intuitive web interface built on NiceGUI. All session state is automatically saved locally in browser storage so your work is preserved across browser refreshes.

docs.title: Top Navigation Header
docs.text:
• Active Model Selector: Switch between different active binding models within the same session.
  • New Model Button: Create a new model configuration from default templates.
  • Export Jupyter Notebook: Download the complete model, imported data, fitting setup, and MCMC pipeline as an offline .ipynb notebook.
  • Save / Load Session: Export/Import the entire session state as JSON.

docs.title: Primary Workspace Tabs
docs.text:
1. Binding Model:
  2. Define chemical components (Host, Guest, Metal, etc.).
  3. Enter equilibrium equations or select fast-exchange analytical models.
  4. Set initial log10(\(K\)) guesses and physical property parameters.
  5. Data Import:
  6. Upload titration data files (CSV, XLSX).
  7. Assign independent variables (total concentrations) and dependent variables (NMR shifts, UV-vis absorbance).
  8. Fitting:
  9. Perform non-linear curve fitting using Levenberg-Marquardt or L-BFGS-B via lmfit.
  10. Inspect fitted parameters, standard errors, \(R^2\), residual plots, and species speciation curves.
  11. Bayes / MCMC:
  12. Configure Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling with emcee.
  13. Set parameter priors (Uniform, Gaussian, Log-Normal).
  14. View chain trace plots and corner plots (corner.py).
  15. Simulation:
  16. Generate synthetic titration data with added Gaussian noise to evaluate model sensitivity and design optimal titration experiments.
